newsitem.title: UK: Euro mogas fleet carrying up to 1 mln tonnes to U.S.
newsitem.headline: Euro mogas fleet carrying up to 1 mln tonnes to U.S.

text.p: An armada of oil tankers carrying gasoline is heading for the oil-thirsty United States from Europe, traders said on Friday.
Between 825,000 and one million tonnes is due to load in January to quench U.S demand.
"More than a cargo a day will be arriving over the next month," said one European gasoline dealer.
"At least 25 tankers have been fixed in the last six working days and there is more to come," said a senior shipbroker in London.
U.S interest for gasoline is currently high as oil companies seek to build stocks ahead of peak consumer demand next summer.

API inventory data published on Wednesday showed gasoline stocks in the U.S at 196 million barrels on January 1, up 4.3 million on a week earlier but significantly 6.5 million barrels down on year ago levels.

Sharp gasoline futures losses on the New York Mercantile Exchange (NYMEX) on Thursday, when February gasoline lost 1.71 cents a gallon to 70.48 cents, were prompted by talk of the lomming European cargoes.
Some European traders on Friday felt the atbitrage window to the U.S has been closed by yesterday's NYMEX losses.
"Its not there any more - there's a lack of ships, very high freight rates and NYMEX has dropped," said one trader.

But others pointed to European prices loosing up to $4 a tonne early on Friday in response to the U.S drop and problems at Tosco's 114,000 barrel a day Bayway refinery cracker. At least two further tankers were understood to be on subjects at midday on Friday.
"There are still ships available and people looking for tonnage, but if they want a big tanker (able to carry 60,000 tonnes) it will have to be late Jan early Feb," said a shipping broker.
Freight rates on 60,000 tonne loads heading transatlantic were assessed at W205 on Friday with 35,000 tonnes put at W255 and 25,000 tonnes at W280.
